title: Chapter 201: Mad Woman
html:
Chen Ge shouted until his throat was raw, but the white cat refused to budge. After several more minutes, he gave up. This cat is too clever. It came over on its own at lunchtime, but the moment I started packing, it ran outside.

He stared up at the tree and sighed helplessly. Slinging on his backpack, he left the park. Night had fallen by the time he reached Fang Hwa Apartments.

I forgot to ask Doctor Gao about this place last time. These buildings are fairly old. I wonder whether anything strange has happened here.

Chen Ge opened the information provided by the police. Patient No. 2 had once been seen here, but the file contained no exact address.

This won’t be easy. The police identify each patient by number, so I don’t even know her name. A photograph isn’t much to work with.

Fang Hwa Apartments was considered an upscale development by Jiujiang standards. Six older buildings stood at the front, dwarfed by three newer towers behind them. Each rose more than twenty stories, and Wang Xin’s family lived in one of the newer buildings.

I should start by asking the security guards.

Chen Ge had come primarily to fulfill the Tape Ghost’s wish and recruit him as an employee. Since he was already here, however, he might as well investigate Patient No. 2.

He approached the security office and showed the guards the photograph Captain Yan had given him. Excuse me, have you seen this woman before?

Every feature of Patient No. 2’s face seemed flawless in isolation, yet together they produced an indefinably wrong impression. Instead of answering, the security guard regarded Chen Ge with suspicion. “You don’t live here, do you?”

“I’m not,” Chen Ge answered honestly.

“Then I don’t have to answer you.” The man stepped out of the office. “If she lives here, we won’t disclose her information. If she doesn’t, I wouldn’t know anything about her anyway.”

The guard’s hostility caught Chen Ge off guard.

“Xiao Gu, don’t be so difficult.” Another guard sat inside, much older than the first. The man, nearly sixty, was changing out of his uniform. He emerged with a chuckle. “Forgive him. He was blamed for something this morning that wasn’t his fault, so he’s in a foul mood.”

“My mood is perfectly fine. Uncle Wong, go home. Your family is waiting. Leave this to me,” the younger guard said impatiently.

“If I leave it to you, you’ll be lectured again tomorrow. You never learn. Would it kill you to be polite to a guest?” Uncle Wong shook his head and sighed. “How many times must I tell you? We’re security guards. Use your hands and feet more than your mouth. Right or wrong, it isn’t our place to judge.”

“It’s all right. I admire his honesty—direct and unpretentious,” Chen Ge said. The young guard struck him as an interesting character. “What should I call you?”

“Gu Feiyu. You can call him Xiao Gu. He’s our night guard—brave and kind, though his mouth has no filter.” Uncle Wong was plainly protective of him.

“Night guard? Do you patrol the complex after dark?” Gu Feiyu was not Chen Ge’s true interest, and he gradually steered the conversation elsewhere.

“We have to keep our tenants safe around the clock.” Uncle Wong brushed dust from his trousers. “You’re looking for someone, right? Tell me her name. I’ve worked here for a decade, so I know practically everyone.”

“I don’t know her name, but I have a photograph.” Chen Ge opened the image and handed over his phone.

“A photograph will be easier.” Uncle Wong took the phone and looked down. The moment he saw the screen, the blood drained from his face, and the device nearly slipped through his fingers.

“You know her?” Chen Ge stepped closer. Uncle Wong thrust the phone back as though it were dangerous.

“This woman is important. She’s connected to several cases.” Chen Ge considered invoking Captain Yan’s name.

“Her again? The police asked about her yesterday.” Gu Feiyu spoke without hesitation.

“What did you tell them?” Chen Ge’s interest sharpened.

Uncle Wong raised a hand to stop Gu Feiyu. His expression grew complicated. “That woman is insane. That’s what I told the police yesterday.”

“Insane?” Chen Ge faced him squarely. “Your reaction wasn’t subtle. She clearly left quite an impression on you.”

“It’s nothing.” More practiced at dealing with people, Uncle Wong offered only part of the truth. “The woman in the photograph called herself Bai, though I suspect that name was false. In person, she looked completely different.”

Fear lingered in Uncle Wong’s eyes. “I remember her because, when she moved into Fang Hwa Apartments two or three years ago, her neighbors complained constantly. A strange smell came from her apartment, and violent arguments erupted at night.”

“That’s all?”

“At first, everything seemed manageable. The landlord spoke with her, and she admitted fault. She apologized and even offered compensation.”

“That hardly makes her insane.” Chen Ge organized the timeline in his head. She had left the Third Sick Hall four years ago, moved into Fang Hwa Apartments three years ago, and disappeared two years ago.

“Two or three months later, rumors spread that her building was haunted. People claimed a white figure appeared in the corridor at midnight.

“Some tenants heard scratching outside their doors at midnight, followed by a woman softly asking, ‘Is anyone home? If no one’s home, I’m coming in.’

“This went far beyond a prank, so the security team was ordered to watch the building. Strangely, whenever we stood guard, neither the white figure nor the woman’s voice appeared. It was as though she were playing hide-and-seek with us.

“We couldn’t maintain the stakeout forever. After two weeks, most of us gave up. The white figure and the voice vanished for an entire month, and we thought it was over. Even so, two guards continued patrolling the building each night.

“During the second month, the guard assigned to patrol with me took emergency leave. I didn’t dare go alone, but then a tenant called to report that the voice had returned. I grabbed my baton and rode the elevator to their floor.

“The moment the elevator opened, I saw a white figure pressed against a nearby door, murmuring, ‘Is anyone home? If no one’s home, I’m coming in.’”

Uncle Wong’s weathered face tightened. Even now, the memory frightened him.

“The white figure was the woman?” Chen Ge could imagine Uncle Wong’s terror.
